author: Latisha Jones
title: Research Analysts’ Updated EPS Estimates for September, 5th (AAPL, BARC, BLUE, CDXS, CRM, EXAS, H, HSBA, KAZ, LLOY)
text:
Tweet
Research Analysts’ updated eps estimates for Wednesday, September 5th:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) had its buy rating reissued by analysts at DA Davidson. The firm currently has a $265.00 target price on the stock. Get Apple Inc alerts:
Barclays (LON:BARC) had its sell rating reissued by analysts at Citigroup Inc. bluebird bio (NASDAQ:BLUE) had its buy rating reissued by analysts at William Blair.
Codexis (NASDAQ:CDXS) had its buy rating reissued by analysts at Craig Hallum. The firm currently has a $20.00 target price on the stock, up from their previous target price of $15.00.
salesforce.com (NYSE:CRM) was upgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a strong-buy rating. They currently have $176.00 target price on the stock. According to Zacks, “Salesforce reported stellar Q2 results and provided a strong outlook. The company’s diverse cloud offerings and strong spending on digital marketing remain the catalysts. Management is extremely optimistic about enhancement of customer experience that has aided growth of the cloud segment. Additionally, strategic acquisitions and the resultant synergies are anticipated to prove conducive to growth over the long run. Furthermore, the company’s move of utilizing other data center operators like Amazon and Alphabet’s geographical reach to expand its international business is commendable and will help it in achieving its targeted $23 billion sales mark by 2022. The stock has outperformed the industry on a year-to-date basis. Nonetheless, stiff competition, currency fluctuations and an increase in investments for international expansions and data centers could negatively impact near-term profitability.”
EXACT Sciences (NASDAQ:EXAS) had its outperform rating reaffirmed by analysts at Cowen Inc. They currently have a $100.00 target price on the stock, up from their previous target price of $65.00.
Hyatt Hotels (NYSE:H) was upgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a buy rating. They currently have $87.00 target price on the stock. According to Zacks, “Shares of Hyatt have outperformed the industry in the past year, owing to better-than-expected earnings in the trailing 10 quarters. The company’s continuous efforts towards expansion, strong brand recognition and acquisition strategies are likely to drive performance in the long run. The company aims to continue gaining market share globally on a solid brand portfolio and innovative personalized service for the guests. Hyatt’s remodeled loyalty program and innovative offerings are expected to boost occupancy. Moreover, an increased focus on expanding presence in the fast-growing select-service category bodes well. Also, earnings estimate for the current year has been revised upward over the past 60 days, reflecting investor’s optimism on the company’s future earnings. However, intense competition is likely to hurt revenues. Also, Hyatt’s weakness in the owned and leased segment is a concern.”
HSBC (LON:HSBA) had its buy rating reissued by analysts at Citigroup Inc.
KAZ Minerals (LON:KAZ) had its outperform rating reissued by analysts at BMO Capital Markets. The firm currently has a GBX 750 ($9.67) target price on the stock.
Lloyds Banking Group (LON:LLOY) had its neutral rating reissued by analysts at Citigroup Inc.
Royal Bank of Scotland Group (LON:RBS) had its buy rating reaffirmed by analysts at Citigroup Inc.
Sappi (OTCMKTS:SPPJY) was downgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a hold rating to a sell rating. According to Zacks, “SAPPI LTD -ADR is the world ‘s leading producer of coated fine paper. They hold major market shares in Europe, North America and Africa. They have customers in over 100 countries worldwide. Their manufacturing operations span eight countries on three continents. “
Standard Chartered (LON:STAN) had its buy rating reissued by analysts at Citigroup Inc.
Atlassian (NASDAQ:TEAM) had its buy rating reiterated by analysts at DA Davidson. The firm currently has a $108.00 price target on the stock.
Veeco Instruments (NASDAQ:VECO) had its hold rating reaffirmed by analysts at Benchmark Co..
Workday (NASDAQ:WDAY) had its buy rating reiterated by analysts at Canaccord Genuity. They currently have a $175.00 price target on the stock, up from their previous price target of $145.00.
